title: PIPE: Estimate the Value of Private Information

source.relative_path: 2018美赛特等奖/F题4篇/F93036-PIPE Estimate the Value of Private Information.pdf

context_sources.name: Steel, Locke, Cadman and Freese, Financial Times personal-data valuation
IBM Cost of Data Breach Study

limitations: Many equations are flattened into running text, especially the demand formula and the similarity definition.
Table 1 rows are misaligned, so several symbols are ambiguous.
Page 4 of the extraction is effectively empty.
The clustering sensitivity metric is defined but its formula is illegible.

tasks: Represent people and queries as feature vectors
Price records with a correlation matrix and a time correction
Build supply and demand at person, group and nation level
Survey privacy law and add a dynamic term
Add a risk-to-benefit factor and compare PI with PP and IP
Cluster social ties and test the value curve
Simulate a breach and assign compensation

section_map.summary: Seven tasks from feature vectors to breach compensation.
Four remedies, privacy kept from the state.
Five categories, no fraud profits, a trusted third party.
Feature vectors, correlation matrix, time amendment.
Benefit-risk demand and three buyer types.
Four measurements, eight subgroups, a logarithm.
Price points, four privacy laws, breach costs.

contributions.summary: A printed correlation matrix with three dominant pairs.
Information that bends as the log of data size.
A breach traced through one ratio to a lower price and a direct liability.

dependency_graph.handoff: The amended data value is what the market prices
The benefit-risk ratio is the channel through which a breach cuts the price
Cluster similarity refines the price inside and between groups

assumptions.summary: All private information falls into a fixed number of categories.
Profits from fraud or harassment are excluded.
A trusted third party holds and sells the data.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Attribute values from the Financial Times, ordinary facts at $0.0005.
600 Facebook users through the Graph API, within platform rules.
Query vectors from a survey of 77 adults.

models.summary: Feature vectors, correlation matrix, exponential amendment.
Benefit-risk demand and a mixture of buyer types.
Four-measurement clustering on an undirected graph.
Breach effect and a retention difference-in-difference.

verification.summary: Eight clustering runs, sensitivity metric from 0.013 to 0.051.
Breach costs by industry and country from IBM.

results_trace.summary: Protection for a year costs about ten times the trade value; a stolen record about $141.
TJX: over 100 million records, $118 million direct loss.

writing_logic.summary: The opening refuses a common belief before stating the gap.
A published report is used to reject linear growth of value.
A breach is traced through one equation to a duty to pay.

language_observations.summary: Each assumption is followed by the consequence that justifies it.
Protection is recast as insurance and priced as a multiple.
A foreign law is refused as a template for a different culture.
Three concepts are separated first and likened second.

visualization_observations.summary: Demand surface over data volume and information entropy.
Figure 1: schematic of the whole pricing framework.
Figure 2: US internet advertising revenue, with an uncertainty band.
Figure 4: information against data size, a logarithm.
Figure 5: six distributions of the PIDATA set.
Figure 6: feature vectors of typical subgroups.
Figure 8: information value across query domains.
Figure 9: data value by country, gray where data are thin.
Figures 10 and 11: breach cost by industry and by region.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The tenfold protection cost is asserted from the IBM figures without the arithmetic shown.
Buyer-type parameters are called estimable but never estimated.
Privacy as a basic human right is a conclusion, not a result.

weaknesses.summary: The correlation matrix and the other parameters need a large dataset the paper does not fully have.
The demand mixture is specified but not fitted.
The similarity formula is too damaged to reproduce.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace the sampled attribute values with a full, sourced database.
Estimate the buyer-type utilities and report them.
Replace the log information curve with a fitted nonlinear predictor.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Make the breaching agency pay the person directly, intent or not.
Let information grow as the log of data size, not linearly.

unresolved_questions.question: What are the fitted buyer-type utilities?
What thresholds and distance weights did the clustering use?
What retention coefficients did the difference-in-difference give?
